items.requirement: The fixture validates and every canonical transition has at least one typed exact basis reference.
Removing or weakening a commit object ID makes the dependent transition invalid.
A branch name alone cannot satisfy an exact-subject requirement.
A machine check bound to commit A cannot unlock the artifact from commit B.
A human-approved transition is accepted when policy permits it, and every generated view labels it as a human-approved assertion with machine_checked: false.
An agent's untyped done assertion cannot satisfy a machine-check gate.
A commit-declared transition request produces no state change until a separate observer event references the immutable resulting commit.
Correcting a transition creates a superseding event and preserves the prior event.
The canonical graph accepts the fixture's legal feedback cycle.
A requires or contains cycle fails the applicable projection.
The roadmap derives locked, available, active, achieved, stale, and blocked nodes with source-level explanations.
AND, OR, and optional prerequisites have distinct, explained unlock semantics.
Every projection carries the same canonical revision or digest.
Editing a generated projection makes the drift check fail.
Bun and Node produce byte-equivalent normalized and derived bounded observations.
The portable core transitive import closure reaches no forbidden capability.
No projection claims more than its evidence category supports under the bounded claim vocabulary.

limitations: This generated artifact maps requirements to commands; it records no command execution or result.
Actual result binding belongs to a separate external commit or CI observation with exact source identity, environment, disposition, output digest, and observation time.
